source_evidence_candidates.exact_quote:
2. One of the objectives of this overview is to "inform the development of a framework for types of
teaching strategies." However, pre-specifying teaching strategies could present potential issues.
For instance, what if the included SRs identify additional teaching strategies? How can you check
that the teaching strategies considered are comprehensive? What criteria were used to develop
the list of teaching strategies, particularly given that some may overlap?

RESPONSE: Thank you. We used a common taxonomy from Beck (that was based on a
review of teacher education textbooks) to initially develop a list of potentially relevant
teaching strategies. We further developed this list iteratively based on literature review and
stakeholder engagement. The protocol provides a comprehensive overview of how the
search strategy and methods were developed.
[external resource identifier omitted]
We agree that there is inherent uncertainty about whether our framework is useful and fully
comprehensive, which is why we stated in the discussion: “…It would be helpful for users of
this research if researchers studying the effects of teaching strategies could reach a
consensus on a taxonomy.”
It was beyond the scope of this review to report on additional teaching strategies that were
not aiming to teach critical thinking.
